National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
1026 AM EDT Mon Oct 19 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Freeze Warnings and Frost Advisories have expired. Higher dew
points and winds tonight will likely preclude frost concerns
where the growing season is still active.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Confidence is increasing that impacts from a nearby
  Nor'easter will be limited this week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Confidence is increasing that impacts from a
nearby Nor'easter will be limited this week.

Overall not too much change in the weather pattern this week. With 
an "Omega Block" taking form, upper-level atmospheric features 
generally remain stuck in place. Current model guidance 
continues to depict ridging over the central US and a strong 
high building over the Great Lakes through the middle of this 
week. Although some uncertainty remains in the exact track of 
the Nor'easter, this pattern tends to keep the developing low 
far enough off the Mid- Atlantic coast to nearly eliminate 
shower potential across our region through next week. Overall, 
any impacts will be tied to coastal communities along the 
Chesapeake Bay where potential minor coastal flooding and gusty 
marine winds remain possible concerns this week. As for these 
marine and coastal flooding concerns see the corresponding 
discussions below. 

Late in the week, this Nor'easter is expected to pull away from the 
coast giving way to another strong high pressure system over our 
area. Heading into next weekend, dry and seasonable conditions are 
expected to persist.

Temperatures this week remain steady with highs in the mid to 
upper 50s and overnight lows in the upper 30s to mid 40s.


&&

.AVIATION /14Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
VFR conditions continue through the week as surface high 
pressure builds overhead and dry conditions persist. Winds 
remain primarily out of the north each day with terminals 
gusting around 15-20 knots in the afternoon. 

&&

.MARINE...
The Nor'easter off the Mid-Atlantic coast will deliver a 
prolonged period of high end SCA conditions and marginal gales 
(mainly over the middle Chesapeake). The Gale Warning continues for
tonight into Tuesday morning from Drum Point to Smith Point and
Tangier Sound. Additionally, Small Craft Advisories are in place 
through Tuesday morning for most of the waters excluding the 
upper Potomac. While the threat for gale force winds diminishes 
after Tuesday, Small Craft Advisories will likely be needed for 
portions of the waters through the end of the week.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies rise through midweek as a Nor'easter lingers
offshore. Tidal locations including Dahlgren, Annapolis,
Solomons Island, and Alexandria are forecast to reach minor
flood stage by Tuesday or Wednesday high tide cycles. However,  
some uncertainty remains on how exactly this Nor'easter will 
track and subsequently affect the tide levels. Elevated water 
levels likely won't decline until late in the week due to the 
stagnant weather pattern.

&&
